title: Terminus: A Programmable Accelerator for Read and Update Operations on Sparse Data Structures
problem: Operations on sparse data structures like hash tables, trees, and compressed tensors are expensive and inefficient on current systems. Prior accelerators either limit supported data structure types or focus only on reads without supporting fine-grained updates.
motivation: Sparse data structures are ubiquitous in modern systems, making efficient acceleration of their operations critical for overall performance.
method: Terminus adds a programmable specialized circuit—a dataflow engine—next to each processor core that can be configured to speed up different types of sparse data operations, like hash table and tree updates, by efficiently managing how data moves. Multiple cores can safely update the same sparse structure at the same time through address-range-based coordination: cores check which memory addresses they need to access, and if those ranges don't overlap, they proceed in parallel without conflicts. Very complex operations that don't fit this approach are delegated to the regular processor cores.
key_novelty: A programmable circuit that speeds up both reading and fine-grained updating of diverse sparse data structures while letting multiple cores work safely through memory-address coordination.
contributions: Programmable dataflow engine extending general-purpose cores for sparse data structure acceleration
Support for both read and update operations on sparse structures, unlike prior accelerators
Address-range-based concurrency control mechanism enabling safe parallel updates
7.4x geometric mean performance improvement over CPU baseline
primary_theme: programmable acceleration for sparse data structures
